Kaluszyn New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Kałuszyn, Poland

Demolished. Jewish settlement in Kałuszyn is confirmed from the second half of the 18th century; by 1921, 5,033 Jews made up 82% of the town, most killed by Germans in 1942, with some survivors murdered even after the war. This cemetery, probably established around 1900, became a wartime execution site - 12 Jews shot in 1941, several hundred to about a thousand murdered in September 1942. Poland formally closed it in 1964, documentation noting it had been abandoned since 1943. Authorities considered converting the site to farmland (1979) and a sports field (1983) before the town office cleaned and fenced it in 1987. In 2017, descendants of Kałuszyn's Jews worked with the Foundation for the Preservation of Jewish Heritage and a US heritage commission to erect a memorial monument.
